issue.title: Make approved-plan persistence single-writer and epic launches source-swap safe
issue.description: Approved tales produce exactly one canonical plan commit before their runner resumes, artifact-link finalization cannot be poisoned by a competing plan writer, and an approved epic waits safely through an in-progress developer update instead of ending as a failed launch with no work started.

issue.title: Make plan approval one atomic publication boundary
issue.description: archive-ownership: establish one host-owned canonical plan archive operation, publish its durable path in the terminal gate response before a planner can resume, retain an explicit compatibility fallback for genuinely old responses, and prove that concurrent approval and runner writers cannot recur.

issue.title: Hold approved epic launches through developer source swaps
issue.description: swap-safe-epic-launch: keep direct bead work fail-fast while making the detached host-owned epic launcher wait outside the editable SASE import boundary, then execute exactly once from a fresh process under the existing code-swap reader protection.

issue.title: Prove the combined approval-to-launch lifecycle
issue.description: reliability-integration: exercise tale approval, sidecar link finalization, epic approval during a developer update, and exhaustive repository checks together so neither fix leaves a false failed agent or a duplicate durable mutation.

payload.entry: PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: Refresh generated SASE memory/provider shims — `just check` currently fails at `sase validate` because `init memory --check` reports 7 generated memory files and provider shims need regeneration; this requires explicit memory-update permission.

Implemented host-owned pre-terminal plan archive publication; verified focused approval/ACE/CLI/poller/runner tests (105 passed), runner follow-up tests (18 passed), just _lint-symvision passed, and just check passed through fmt/ruff/mypy/lints/symvision/toobig but failed at SASE validation init memory --check due generated memory/provider shims requiring refresh; recorded PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP on this bead.
PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: just check SASE validation still fails at init memory --check (chezmoi home shim drift, same 7 files already tracked on sase-n0) — this phase did not regenerate memory.
PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: tests/main/test_skills_handler.py::test_skills_inventory_reports_retired_deletion_drift fails under xdist (already tracked on sase-rv) — unrelated to swap-safe epic launch.

Host-owned epic launches wait in a stdlib bootstrap (no sase import) for the code-swap shared lock, then exec sase bead work once while the lock is held. Direct sase bead work still fail-fast (test_cli_work_code_swap_lock). Monitor and fallback-proc paths share guarded execution argv while labels/fingerprints/resume commands stay logical sase bead work; sidecar persists execution argv for restart. 62 focused tests passed; lint (fmt/ruff/mypy/symvision/toobig) passed; no --epic-symbol leftovers. just check validate is blocked by pre-existing sase-n0 chezmoi memory drift; test-scoped 4954 passed with one pre-existing sase-rv failure.

Added combined approval-to-launch regressions (tale delayed-archive + coder link linear history; epic code-swap wait then one DAG). Verified combined approval-to-launch regressions: tale delayed-archive + coder artifact-link linear history; historical two-writer rebase conflict; inverted-scheduling archive publication; epic code-swap wait then one DAG. DISCOVERED ISSUE: During cli_detail.py module-split verification on 2026-08-22, required just check escalated to the full suite and deterministically failed the plan-approval gate/action cluster. An isolated rerun of tests/test_plan_auto_approval.py::test_handle_plan_approval_auto_approve failed identically: archive_approved_plan cannot resolve a project from action-data keys [bundle_path, original_plan_file, plan_tier, request_id, request_kind, response_dir, session_id]. The local diff only reorganizes bead-detail rendering modules; this independently corroborates this epic's approval-publication scope.

Verified epic completion end to end. Reviewed the epic notes plus every note on closed children sase-s2.1, sase-s2.2, and sase-s2.3; audited the implementation and tests in commits 209375b22 (atomic approved-plan archive publication), f8a0dd858 (launch hold through developer source swaps), and 62538c4b0 (combined lifecycle proof). The two later DISCOVERED ISSUE reports on sase-s2 were the pre-fix archive_approved_plan project-resolution failure and are addressed by sase-s2.1; the focused approval/archive/runner/code-swap/monitor/epic-launch lane passed 230 tests. Reviewed post-start non-epic commits c718da911, b05d2d5b, e52cc27d, 104e02e4, c4413856, e674ffc6, and cf72b00d and found no duplicated implementation, conflict, or missing consumer. While landing, fast-forwarded and reviewed newly landed bcffb4a72, 5507cc069, and a22ca4d61: wait-status presentation and bead-detail splitting remain orthogonal, while 5507cc069 supplies the independently owned contract-manifest correction discovered during this audit. Follow-up outcomes: sase-s2.1 memory drift did not reproduce under either .venv/bin/sase validate or .venv/bin/sase init memory --check --diff, so proposed duplicate sase-n0 was declined; sase-s2.2 skills-inventory xdist drift passed with -n 2 and serial, so proposed duplicate sase-rv was declined; sase-s2.3 contract-manifest drift reproduced from c718da911, was corroborated on sase-iu and recorded on causally owning epic sase-s1, then fixed by integrated commit 5507cc069; ready duplicate sase-n3 was closed superseded because sase-s2 provides the verified fix. Exhaustive just check-full reached 36044 passes and exposed only that already-routed contract drift, 28 parity failures caused by an absent local sase-xprompt-lsp executable, and the known unrelated xdist UI timeout. After installing the required LSP dependency and integrating 5507cc069, all 30 previously failing nodes passed in a focused serial rerun. The UI timeout also passed immediately on the unchanged pre-fast-forward tree and was recorded as an artifact-backed independent report on exact duplicate flake sase-qr using file:explicit:e42d6f43c065467bda237dfe. sase bead epic-symbols sase-s2 reported no entries. No epic-caused work remains.
